title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Zweiphasiger städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Wettbewerb nach RPW 2013 - Produktives Quartier Gutleut-West
description: Gegenstand des Wettbewerbes ist ein städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Entwurf in dem gezeigt wird, wie die Transformation eines gewerblich geprägten Bestandsareals zu einem nutzungsgemischten, klimaangepassten und gemeinwohlorientierten Quartier gelingen kann. In einer Stadt mit hoher Flächennachfrage und begrenzten innerstädtischen Entwicklungsreserven treffen hier Ansprüche unmittelbar aufeinander, die sich andernorts oft räumlich aus dem Weg gehen: Wohnen und Gewerbe, Logistik und Aufenthalt, soziale Infrastruktur und Produktion, Freiraum und Verdichtung. Die entscheidende Frage lautet deshalb nicht, welche Nutzung sich am Ende durchsetzt. Interessanter ist, wie aus dieser Konkurrenz ein Stück Stadt entstehen kann. Aufgabe des Wettbewerbs ist es, eine eigene räumliche Antwort zu entwickeln. Gesucht wird vornehmlich nicht das möglichst vollständige Bild eines irgendwann „fertigen“ Gutleut-West. Gesucht wird vielmehr ein städtebauliches und freiraumplanerisches Gerüst, das Orientierung gibt, ohne Entwicklung einzuschränken. Es soll durch zu entwickelnde Prinzipien Qualitäten sichern und zugleich Spielräume eröffnen – für unterschiedliche Nutzungen, Träger:innen, Eigentümer:innen und Entwicklungszeitpunkte. Die Ausloberin beabsichtigt, unter Würdigung der Empfehlung des Preisgerichts, das mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichnete Team mit der Ausarbeitung des Wettbewerbsergebnisses zu beauftragen. Die Ausloberin wird hierzu ein Verhandlungsverfahren ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb gemäß § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 VgV durchführen. Dabei behält sich die Ausloberin vor, das Verhandlungsverfahren zunächst nur mit dem mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichneten Team durchzuführen. Scheitern diese Verhandlungen oder besteht ein wichtiger Grund, der einer Beauftragung des 1. Preisträgers entgegensteht, werden die weiteren Preisträger zur Teilnahme an den Verhandlungen aufgefordert. Das Wettbewerbsergebnis wird im anschließenden Vergabeverfahren als Zuschlagskriterium mit 60 % gewichtet. Die Rangfolge der Preisträger gemäß der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts wird dabei entsprechend berücksichtigt, d.h. der 1. Preisträger erhält im Kriterium ‚Wettbewerbsergebnis' die höchste Punktzahl, der 2. Preisträger die zweithöchste usw. Die weitere Bearbeitung umfasst den städtebaulichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 51 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie den freiräumlichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 52 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie die Erstellung eines "Qualitätshandbuchs". Eine darüberhinausgehende Beauftragung weiterer Planungsleistungen bleibt vorbehalten und ist nicht Bestandteil dieses Auftragsversprechens. Ziel ist die Erarbeitung eines Rahmenplans mit integrierter Freiraumplanung als Vorstufe zum Bebauungsplan nach BauGB sowie als Grundlage für das im Anschluss geplante Konzeptverfahren für die hochbauliche Entwicklung auf den Baufeldern. Die Preisträger:innen verpflichten sich, im Falle einer Beauftragung durch die Ausloberin, die weitere Bearbeitung zu übernehmen und durchzuführen. Im Zuge der Überarbeitung der Wettbewerbsergebnisse treten sie mit der Bürgerschaft und Schlüsselpersonen vor Ort im Rahmen von Dialogformaten in Austausch (z.B. Vorstellung des Wettbewerbs-Ergebnisses, Rückfragenbeantwortung, Aufnahme von Hinweisen für weitere Bearbeitung). Die Beauftragung erfolgt vorbehaltlich des Abschlusses des erforderlichen Vergabeverfahrens, der erforderlichen haushaltsrechtlichen Voraussetzungen, der Eignung des Teilnehmers sowie des Vorliegens eines wichtigen Grundes, der einer Beauftragung entgegensteht. Im Falle einer weiteren Bearbeitung werden durch den Wettbewerb bereits erbrachte Leistungen des Preisträgers bis zur Höhe des zuerkannten Preises nicht erneut vergütet, wenn und soweit der Wettbewerbsentwurf unverändert der weiteren Bearbeitung zugrunde gelegt wird.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Center for Neutron Research (NCNR) owns and operates a 20 MW test reactor called the National Bureau of Standards Reactor (NBSR) located in Gaithersburg, Maryland. The NBSR is fueled by 30 highly enriched uranium fuel elements. During the course of a year, the NBSR produces approximately 28 spent fuel elements. To be in accordance with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), NIST is required to transfer its spent fuel to the Department of Energy (DOE) Savannah River Site (SRS) near Aiken, South Carolina. This requirement is for one base shipment to be completed no later than December 31, 2028, with an option for a second shipment to be completed no later than December 31, 2030. See attached solicitation# 1333ND27QNB610AMD and related attachments for full details.

title: Solid-State Energy Conversion from Heat to Electricity Request for Information (RFI)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Defense Sciences Office (DSO) is requesting information on the current state of the art and technological limitations of solid-state direct thermal-to-electric energy conversion technologies. We define solid state energy conversion as systems that convert a temperature differential directly into electrical energy without utilizing mechanical moving parts (e.g., pistons, turbines, or rotary alternators). This RFI seeks to identify the best possible solid state heat engine performance across a wide operating temperature range, factors that limit performance, and the most attractive use cases if these highly efficient solid state heat engines could be made today. This survey of limits, challenges and use cases will identify opportunities for research and development to inform potential program(s) in this area.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN or Contract Number: 87758 Approximate Estimate: $9,300,000 Anticipated Posting: January 2027 Description: Remediation of PFAS-impacted soils at CFB Comox through in-situ soil mixing (chemical) and stabilization, selective excavation, off-site disposal, drainage improvements, and site restoration. The work is located within a former detonation and training area and is subject to UXO risk, environmental protection requirements, and tight seasonal construction windows. Construction will be completed in two distinct phases due to schedule constraints, UXO sequencing, and constructability considerations. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. title: Design-Build Renovation of Building 164, Outdoor Recreation Center, Homestead Air Reserve Base, Florida
description: The Department of the Air Force intends to award a firm-fixed-price design-build construction contract for renovation of the Outdoor Recreation Facility, Building 164, at Homestead Air Reserve Base, Florida. The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, transportation, design and engineering services, tools, permits, testing, inspections, quality control, warranties, and closeout documentation necessary to complete the work in accordance with the solicitation, Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and all attachments. The requirement includes design-build services for renovation and improvement of Building 164. Work includes, but is not limited to, preparation of design documents; demolition; roofing and exterior-envelope improvements; doors, windows, exterior walls, and drainage work; interior renovations; mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and lighting work; site improvements; testing; inspections; warranties; and closeout documentation. The solicitation will include a base requirement consisting of Phases 1 and 2 and a separately priced Option 1 for Phase 3. The specific requirements for the base requirement and Option 1 are identified in Section B and the Statement of Work. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Size Standard: $45.0 Million Average Annual Receipts PSC: Y1JZ � Construction of Miscellaneous Buildings Place of Performance: Homestead Air Reserve Base Building 164 Homestead, Florida Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price, Design-Build Construction Magnitude of Construction: Between $250,000 and $500,000 Period of Performance: 360 calendar days after issuance of the Notice to Proceed. SITE VISIT: A site visit will be held on 10 November 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time. Attendance is strongly encouraged but is not mandatory. Offerors planning to attend shall submit the completed base-access form no later than 5 November 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time. At this time, Homestead Air Reserve Base is processing site-visit access requests for United States citizens only. Site-visit directions and additional access information will be provided to approved attendees. Offerors that do not attend the site visit remain responsible for becoming familiar with existing conditions, site access restrictions, facility operations, utility conditions, material-staging limitations, and all other conditions that may affect performance. QUESTIONS: Questions concerning this solicitation shall be submitted in writing to Tahj Guilford at tahj.guilford.2@us.af.mil no later than 13 November 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time. Questions received after the stated deadline may not be answered. The Government anticipates posting responses to timely submitted questions on or about 18 November 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION: Offerors shall submit proposals electronically to tahj.guilford.2@us.af.mil no later than 23 November 2026 at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Proposals shall be submitted in the format required by Sections L and M of the solicitation. Offerors are responsible for ensuring proposals are received by the Government before the closing date and time. The Government intends to make award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussions if determined to be in the Government�s best interest. All amendments to this solicitation will be posted through SAM.gov. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments and acknowledging all amendments with their proposal. title: Canonsburg-Houston, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District, has a project as the Canonsburg-Houston Local Protection Project (LPP) is an authorized federal flood damage reduction project spanning over 20,500 linear feet of channel improvements along Chartiers Creek. Originally constructed by USACE in two phases (Houston unit completed in 1970; Canonsburg unit completed in 1976), operation and maintenance responsibilities were subsequently transferred to Washington County. Severe storm events resulted in substantial damage to the channel embankment along the right bank of Chartiers Creek, including displacement of stone protection and loss of subgrade stabilization. This rehabilitation contract encompasses repair and re-armoring of the degraded channel reach to restore federal project integrity and design conveyance capacity. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $150,000.00 and $350,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The anticipated award date is 11 December 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO Part 13 and 36, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that are unrealistically low or exceed available funds for this requirement. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/ then scrolling down on right hand side of page by clicking on View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

title: Service Order Desk
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT FOR SOLUTION BASED CAPABILITY STATEMENTS ONLY. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) - Fort Carson, CO, in coordination with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW), is seeking Solution based capability statement for an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Market Research purposes. The requirement is to design, integrate, test, deploy, and support a modernized, commercial Service Order Desk Platform. The core objective is to decouple the Service Order Desk from the legacy Base Operations contract, transitioning it into an independent, highly automated, data-transparent, and user-centric platform. Successful solutions must deliver 100% auditable real-time tracking of funds by facility type, establish direct digital pathways with the Army Maintenance Application (ArMA) without manual data re-entry, and prevent premature ticket closures via multi-state tracking and parallel POC notifications.. Security compliance requires deployment in a secure Department of War (DOW) Impact Level 5 (IL5) cloud environment featuring Role-Based Access Control and CAC/SSO integration . Submissions must be Solution Based Capability Statement not exceeding 10 pages and must be submitted by Monday, November 23, 2026, at 10:00 AM MT to Jessica Smith (Jessica.l.smith499.civ@army.mil), Frank Camacho (frank.m.camacho.civ@army.mil), and MAJ Ryan Lee (jong.d.lee2.mil@army.mil)

title: AFP for Lease of Discovery Park at Michoud Assembly Facility
description: This Announcement for Proposals (AFP) solicits proposals for lease of Discovery Park which represents a selection of available real property assets at MAF. The real property assets (The Property) known as Discovery Park, and shown in Exhibit A, are as follows: 1. Approximately 45 Acres of Greenspace: This tract of land lies on the northern extent of the facility and is bounded by Old Gentilly Road (publicly accessible roadway) as well as Mercury, Uranus and Venus Drives, which are interior to the security fencing. The acreage is currently classified as underutilized greenspace. The tract�s frontage to Old Gentilly Road has availability to direct connection with municipal power, potable water and sewer services. These utilities may be established with each respective service carrier. Please see Exhibit B for a listing of municipal resources which may assist in performing diligence for these service agreements. The acreage includes what were previously large sections of parking areas that supported a previously demolished building. These areas are past their useful service life and thus have been considered greenspace for appraisal purposes. 2. Building 351: Building 351 is an approximately 32,000 sf mixed used facility. The building is subdivided into two main areas: formal event space and cafeteria. The building currently is connected to the MAF utility grids. As a result, some determination will need to be made with respect to severing the building from those utilities and re-establishing utility services from the previously mentioned municipal service providers based upon the proposer�s concept of use. This reconfiguration would be made subject to NASA�s approval and terms of use. The Proposer may choose to propose on either asset separately or a combination of the two. NASA shall have the authority to execute either one or multiple leases in the event The Proposer chooses to include a combination of both assets in their submission. NASA intends to utilize Enhanced Use Lease authority as set forth in 51 U.S.C. 20145 as the sole means to enter into a lease(s) for The Property. The Proposer will assume any and all financial responsibilities for operations and maintenance of The Property under such a lease. The terms and conditions in the attached Model Enhanced Use Lease (EUL) generally demonstrate all the Proposer responsibilities including those maintenance and operational parameters. While The Property has existing utilities which serve other portions of the facility, the Proposer should not assume that any existing utilities will be available for use and that any utilities required for development will be at the sole cost of the Proposer. The Property will be available at award in �as is� condition for no less than one ten (10) year base term. title: Float Well Pipe Repairs, Surry Mountain Dam, Surry, NH
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Construction Services for the for the repairing of the inlet pipe to the float well and replace weathered/damaged staff gauges at the Surry Moutain Lake Dam in Surry NH. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990 with a size standard of $45M. The project is planned to be solicited in the Winter of 2026 with construction to begin place in the Summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $350,000 - $500,000. The project site is the inlet culvert on the lake side of the Surry Mountain Dam in Surry, NH. Work for this project will likely include, but not be limited to, the following: Coffer dam at inlet pipe location. Float well pipe (3-inch cast iron) cleaning. Installation of internal liner for float well pipe. Pre and Post liner installation CCTV inspections. Repairs to the slash-zone pipe segment Protection and concrete encasement of the external float well pipe Staff Gauges: Pressure treated posts with attached enamel coated metal measuring strip. Scheduled work will be affected by depth of pool. Assumed low pool depths are July and August (when work can be conducted safely), but adverse weather conditions (rain events) could delay or postpone work schedules. Surry Mountain staff will keep COR informed of pool levels to anticipate when work can commence if outside assumed low pool depths. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. Please include at least two specific examples of the firm�s experience performing the work requirements stated above. The projects must have been performed within the last seven years. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications, which will be used to support the offeror�s effort, and their experience must also have been performed within the last seven years. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages. Responses are due by 21 September 2026. Responses should be emailed to: Kyle Hall � kyle.k.hall@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8479 Interested firms shall provide the above documentation in one original form and one copy. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. title: USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA) Request for Proposal(s)
description: The Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) issues solicitation amendment N00024-26-R-4421 A0003 for the execution of the USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA). This Signature Availability includes a combination of maintenance, modernization, and repair, and will require highly capable contractors with substantial facilities, to include capable pier (for the applicable ship class) as well as human resources capable of completing, coordinating, and integrating multiple areas of ship maintenance, repair and modernization. This Signature Availability is solicited on a coast-wide basis on the West Coast under a single solicitation, and one (1) contract to complete the availability is expected to be awarded to one (1) contractor. Based on the complexity, magnitude and duration of the requirement, the Governments market research indicates there are not two or more small business concerns capable of competing for these requirements and therefore this procurement will not be set aside for small business (FAR 19.502-2(b)). This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested parties must comply with this announcement. Interested offerors should monitor the PlEE.gov and SAM.gov pages for the release of the solicitation and any applicable amendments, thereafter. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to participate in this procurement at https://www.sam.gov. All responsible sources may submit a proposal, which shall be considered by the agency. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. Potential offerors will need to request access to all applicable CDRLs, J- and S- attachments by providing a written request to the Contract Specialist, Jacob Juros at jacob.a.juros.civ@us.navy.mil and the Contracting Officer, Brian Romano, at brian.c.romano.civ@us.navy.mil. Include your companys SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number with the request so that contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. These attachments will be transmitted via DoD SAFE. ***NOTICE*** In addition, there are references that contain limiting distribution statements and will not be disseminated from the Contract Specialist. In these instances, Offerors shall contact the Southwest Regional Maintenance Center (SWRMC) Technical Librarian at swrmc.techdocs@us.navy.mil to arrange access per RFP Section L instruction. Offerors shall review Section L, General Information for further details. ***END NOTICE***The Government anticipates making a single award in or before March 2027. USS MAKIN ISLAND (LHD 8) FY28 DSRA will begin in November 2027 with an expected completion in October 2029. *****A0001***** The purpose of this amendment is as follows:1) Update Section B, Note A to reflect updated Attachment J-4 direct labor hours and fully burdened materials,2) Updated Section B, Note E growth occurrences and SDVG total available incentive amount to align with updated Attachment J-4,3) Updated Section B, Note H to aligned with Attachment J-3s Contract Complete date of 30 October 2029 vice 02 October 2026.4) Updated Section C, Scope of Work Paragraph 1.7 A-Dates to match Paragraph 1.2s dates,5) Updated Section I, 52.211-11 Liquidated Damages to reflect standard NAVSEA language regarding Contract Complete milestone,6) Updated Section J to reserve Attachment S-10 and update Attachments J-1 to include ERRATA 1,7) Updated Section J to update Attachments J-4, J-8, and J-10 in response to ERRATA 1,8) To provide answers to Bidders Questions (PPIs).Any other updates indicated on the SF-30 are a result of formatting changes or contract writing system updates. *****A0002***** The purpose of this amendment is as follows:1) To update Attachment J-1 to incorporate ERRATA 2, cancelling work items as specified in the Cancelled Work Specs List attached,2) To update Attachments J-3, J-4, J-8, J-9, and J-10 to reflect cancelled work items as part of ERRATA 2,3) To provide Government responses to Bidders Questions. ***** A0003 ***** The purpose of this amendment is to: 1) Extend proposal receipt/due date 2 weeks to 23 November 2026 from 9 November 2026, 2) Incorporate ERRATA 3 into Attachment J-1, 3) Provide answers to Bidders Questions.

title: DOWEA Preventative Maintenance Demand Maintenance- Puerto Rico IDIQ
description: W91236 27X1CTA Sources Sought Notice DOWEA Preventative Maintenance Demand Maintenance- Puerto Rico IDIQ at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla This is a Sources Sought Notice only; it is not a request for competitive proposals. There is no solicitation, specifications, and/or drawings available at this time. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to identify business concerns with sufficient similar experience that are capable and interested in performing the work described herein. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any cost incurred in preparation of a response to this notice. The Government intends to use responses to this Sources Sought to make appropriate acquisition decisions for the project. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought notice. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Norfolk District is anticipating a new procurement for a Firm-Fixed Price Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Services contract, for the Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) Preventative Maintenance (PM) and Demand Maintenance (DM) at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. Description of Work USACE, Norfolk District is seeking eligible firms capable of Preventative Maintenance and Demand Maintenance repair services in support of the DoWEA-America�s facilities located at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. The services provided under this proposed contract encompass facilities total maintenance services such as operation and maintenance of heating, ventilation and cooling systems, kitchen equipment, facility control systems, playgrounds, plumbing, electrical, and fire alarms, building systems, roofs, and other facility systems and components. These services must be provided on an ongoing basis without protracted lapse to ensure that the building systems continue to operate efficiently and safely for the benefit of the students and teachers that inhabit them. The facilities under this action which require Preventative Maintenance & Demand Repair Maintenance include a total of five (5) buildings comprised of three (3) schools and one (1) support facility at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan for an approximate total of 320,870 GSF; and one (1) Ramey Unit School at Aguadilla for an approximate total of 122,539 GSF. Solicitation Anticipated solicitation issuance timeframe is on or about January 2027, and the estimated solicitation period of 30 calendar days with a proposal due date timeframe on or about February 2027. The project consists of a 12-month base period, four (4) option years for a total of five (5) years. NAICS Code 238220 - Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors applies with a Small Business Size Standard of $19,000,000.00 Offerors will be evaluated on a Best-Value Tradeoff basis with a combination of price and non-price factors. All interested firms shall be registered in SAM.GOV and PIEE in order to submit a proposal in response to the solicitation when issued. VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE The Government will host a Virtual Industry Day to engage with interested parties and address questions related to this requirement. Participation in the Virtual Industry Day is voluntary and is not required to submit a capabilities statement. The Virtual Industry Day will be held on Monday, 16 NOV 2026 from 0900-1000 AM Eastern Standard Time (EST). A Microsoft Teams meeting invite will be provided to interested firms who RSVP by email no later than 12 NOV 2026 to Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil and Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INDUSTRY All interested, capable, qualified, and responsive SMALL BUSINESS Prime Contractors are encouraged to reply to this Sources Sought announcement. Interested contractors should furnish the following information: Company name, address, phone number, and point of contact information. Indicate business size in relation to the NAICS Code 238220. Provide your company's Unique Entity Identification number (UEI) to verify your business status as a qualified Small Business (SB), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned SB (SDVOSB), Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZones), Qualified Section 8(a), Women-Owned or other than Small Business. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at time of proposal submission and contract award. Please see www.SAM.gov for additional registration information. Provide a narrative describing primary business lines and the geographic regions your company serves. Narratives shall be no longer than five (5) pages demonstrating experience in a similar type of work as described above, at similar contract values, and in similar locations. Does your company, through in-house forces or subcontract support, have the technical capability and capacity to provide preventive maintenance and demand maintenance repair services for the facilities and locations as described above? Given the Facility Coverage requirements listed in the description of work: what level of staffing would you suggest for full-time employees to be on-site (full time) to fulfill these requirements. Please include the trades as well as the personnel�s pertinent certifications/licenses. The Government intends to include a Limit of Liability (LOL) in this contract for repairs the Contractor would be responsible for under the firm-fixed price portion of this contract. The Contractor�s limit of liability (LoL) for material and labor costs associated with any single demand maintenance event including repair or replacement of any single piece of equipment is $20,000 without limit of maintenance occurrences per year. The Government will utilize this information in determining an Acquisition Strategy. Please submit capability packages electronically via email to Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil and copy Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. The capability statement must be submitted not later than 23 NOV 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). This Sources Sought should not be construed in any manner to be an obligation of USACE, Norfolk District to issue a contract, or result in any claim for reimbursement of costs for any effort you expend responding to this request. All information submitted will be considered procurement sensitive and is being used as a market research tool only. No solicitation is currently available. All prospective contractors are required to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to proposal submission and award. Offerors and contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the Internet at https://www.SAM.gov. Representations and Certifications Applications apply to this solicitation. Representations and Certifications may be completed online via SAM.gov. The Point of Contact for this requirement is Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil, and Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. TELEPHONE INQUIRES WILL NOT BE HONORED.

RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). title: Industry Day - Tactical Protective Equipment
description: SPECIAL NOTICE INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT � TACTICAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT FEDERAL BUREAU OF PRISONS This is a Special Notice issued solely for informational and market research purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a solicitation, nor does it commit the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with participation in this event. 1. Agency and Location Department of Justice Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) 400 First Street NW Washington, DC 20534 Rooms A/B/C 2. Event Description The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) hereby announces an Industry Day for Tactical Protective Equipment, to be conducted December 2�3, 2026, between 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM EST each day. The purpose of this event is to obtain information from industry regarding current products, technologies, and capabilities relevant to protective tactical equipment used in correctional emergency response operations. Information obtained will support the BOP�s national contracting initiative beginning in Fiscal Year 2027. 3. Categories of Equipment for Demonstration Interested vendors shall be prepared to bring physical items for in?person demonstration. Equipment categories include, but are not limited to: � Protective helmets, including riot helmets with face shields � Riot and disturbance control shields � Shin guards and lower?leg protection � Knee and elbow pads � Tactical uniforms � Forearm and upper?arm protection � Chest, shoulder, back, and torso protection � Full?body protective suits and modular protective systems � Tactical vests (Threat Level III?A), including ballistic plate inserts � Protective gloves, including puncture?resistant products � Riot batons and associated accessories � Equipment storage, transport, and maintenance accessories � Other related protective equipment designed for correctional emergency response operations 4. Vendor Participation Requirements To participate, vendors must comply with the following: a. RFI Response Requirement Vendors must submit a response to the associated Request for Information (RFI) identifying: � The desire to attend Industry Day, and � The list of specific equipment proposed for demonstration. Only vendors responding to the RFI will be assigned a time slot. b. RSVP Deadline All RFI responses/RSVPs must be received no later than November 23, 2026, at 2:00 PM EST. Late submissions may not be considered. c. Presentation Time Each vendor will be assigned a presentation period not to exceed one hour. (An additional 30 minutes may be allowed for set-up/break down of equipment.) d. AI/SI Disclosure Requirement Any presentation materials generated using artificial intelligence or synthetic intelligence (AI/SI) must include a disclosure statement positioned at the bottom of each slide. e. Equipment Transport and Restrictions � Vendors shall hand-carry or transport their equipment themselves. � No equipment shall be shipped to the BOP facility. � All items must be non?weaponized and free of ammunition, chemical agents, OC products, pyrotechnics, or operational electronic discharge devices. � Vendors are responsible for setup, handling, and removal of their own equipment. f. Facility Support and Limitations � The Government will provide tables, electricity, extension cords, and display space. � Vendors must provide their own display stands, mannequins, or mounting equipment. � Internet access will not be available. � Vendor personnel must present valid government?issued identification for facility access. 5. Purpose and Disclaimer This Industry Day is intended to enhance the Government�s understanding of current market capabilities and product availability. Participation is voluntary and does not affect future procurement opportunities. Information received may be used for planning purposes only and will not be released outside the Government. 6. Point of Contact All inquiries and RSVP information shall be directed to: Kasie Redman Contracting Officer Federal Bureau of Prisons Email: k2redman@bop.gov

title: Manufacture of M284A2 155mm and other MTC Cannon Tubes
description: Purpose: The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island (ACC-RI) at Picatinny, Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806-5000 is conducting a Market Survey on behalf of the Project Manager Howitzer Systems (PM-HS). PM-HS has a need to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing the M284A2 155mm, and other 155mm cannon tubes domestically in specific quantities and lead time annotated below. The purpose of this market research is to obtain current information on the capability of additional sources to manufacture 155mm Cannon Tubes up to 30-foot length. No other data or drawings will be provided with this Market Survey. Description: The .39 caliber, 155-mm M776 and M284A2 cannon tubes are components of the M777A2 and M109A6/A7 Howitzers respectively. 155-mm cannons are direct support cannon fire support system for the U.S. Army and must be built to the United States Government technical data specifications. This Sources Sought is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the US Government. All interested respondents are requested to provide a written response summarizing the following capabilities and organizational details. Manufacturers with domestic capacity in the works are also encouraged submit their response along with their prospective production timetables. Please clarify if respondent�s capabilities apply to one or all the cannon tube models. REQUESTED: 1. Name of company, address, telephone number, email address, technical point of contact, CAGE code, UEI, and business size information (please specify as either a Large Business, Foreign-Owned Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a) concern, Woman-Owned Small Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone concern, Veteran-Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Small Business). 2. Experience: A description of the respondent�s manufacturing experience of the 155-mm Cannon Tubes, or similar products, within the last five (5) years to include past performance. Include applicable description of experience with each cannon tube. 3. Production Process: A description of the respondent�s existing 155-mm cannon production process to include all major manufacturing stages and the operations/equipment utilized for each, as well as all supporting subcontractors. The description must detail the entire production lifecycle, including, but not limited to: 3.1. A detailed description of the respondents bore and outside diameter cold working capabilities to include autofrettage. 3.2. A detailed description of the respondent�s boring and milling capabilities along with the capacity or each (length, weight, outer/inner diameters). 3.3. A detailed description of the respondent's rifling capabilities, including methods (e.g., swage, broach, or single-point machining) and general experience with standard 155-mm rifling configurations (lands, grooves, and twist rates). 3.4. A detailed description of the respondent or subcontractor coating capabilities for chrome bore coatings on a steel tube up to 30 ft long and up to 7,500 pounds in weight. Provide the maximum length and weight of tube that can be coated by respondent. 3.5. A detailed description of the respondent�s protective coating and painting capabilities. 3.6. Detailed description of the respondent�s advanced manufacturing capabilities and growth areas. 4. Production Capacity: A description of the respondent�s current maximum monthly capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes. Please specify separate production rate capacity for each and if different manufacturing lines, tooling, or subcontractors are utilized. 5. Production Availability: A description of the respondent�s maximum caliber capability and projected available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes within 18 months from the date of these sources sought. 6. Optimization opportunity: A description of the domestic facilities, equipment, machines and tooling required to increase the available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes up to ten (10) tubes per month, regardless of caliber, within 36 months from the date of this source sought. Specify whether the projected production capacity for each tube type is dedicated or shared across multiple lines. Provide an NTE ROM cost estimate for an initial production quantity of forty (40) cannon tubes (broken down by caliber or indicating pricing for a combined/flexible mix). 7. Material: A detailed description of the respondent�s cannon tube source material grade, respondent(s) and processing. Such as, but not limited to, steel preform production, forging, guide bore, and heat treatment. All companies interested in this notice must be registered and valid in System for Award Management (SAM). This market survey is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a Request for Proposal (RFP). All information is to be submitted at no cost or obligation to the Government. If a future formal Government requirement is generated, a solicitation notice will be published. Please identify, with markings, proprietary information submitted. All respondents� information provided will not be returned, will hold in confidential status, and destruction notice shall be provided. All market information sought in this notification must be provided within 30 days of this notice by electronic mail only at no cost to the Government.

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. title: B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR) - Buy and Repair F3I DTR
description: B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR) The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources with the expertise, capabilities, experience, facilities, and technical capacity necessary to manufacture/provide and repair the B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR). The National Stock Number (NSN) and Part Number (PN) are as follows: LRU: NSN 7025-01-738-4504AY, P/N P210015K0001-1, INTERFACE UNIT, DATA This Request for Information (RFI) supports a buy and repair requirement for the new Form, Fit, Function, and Interface (F3I) DTR. Kihomac, Inc. is currently manufacturing the F3I DTR under contract SPRWA1-21-D-0015. The Government owns, or will provide under appropriate controls, the manufacturing and technical data necessary to support competitive production and repair of this item. The Government intends to compete this requirement on the open market to obtain new production units and repair services. The legacy B-52 DTR is repaired by Symetrics Industries (CAGE 22830) under contracts FA8539-20-D-0013 and FA8539-25-D-0004. This market research effort pertains to the F3I DTR identified above, currently being manufactured by Kihomac, Inc. under contract SPRWA1-21-D-0015, and is intended to identify sources capable of supporting competitive manufacture and repair using Government-owned technical data. The DTR is a Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) on the B-52 aircraft, with two DTRs installed per aircraft. The DTR transfers Offensive Avionics System (OAS) information to and from storage on the Data Transfer Cartridge (DTC) across its interface with the Fibre Channel or MIL-STD-1553A data bus system. Additionally, the DTR provides status over the MIL-STD-1553A and Fibre Channel buses indicating that the DTC is successfully installed. The required scope shall include, as applicable, manufacture and delivery of new production DTR units; hardware repair and return of unserviceable DTR units; obsolete parts resolution; engineering support to investigate Deficiency Reports (DRs); Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) support; development, maintenance, and execution of required inspection, test, and acceptance procedures; and configuration management support to ensure newly manufactured and repaired units conform to the applicable Government-furnished technical data package. All newly manufactured and repaired units must meet applicable form, fit, function, and interface requirements. The contractor shall furnish all necessary material, support equipment, tools, test equipment, facilities, and services required to perform the work. The contractor is responsible for acquiring, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at its primary or subcontractor facilities. Contractor-furnished material or replacement parts must equal or exceed the quality, tolerances, and specifications identified in the applicable technical data package. INSTRUCTIONS: 1. The document(s) below contain a description of the NSN listed for buy and repair requirements and a Contractor Capability Survey. The Survey allows Contractors to provide their company�s capability. 2. If, after reviewing these documents, you wish to participate in this market research, you should provide documentation demonstrating your company's capability to meet these buy and repair requirements. Failure to provide adequate documentation may prevent the government from properly assessing your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please explain how you would overcome this deficiency to fulfill the requirement (e.g., through teaming or subcontracting). a. Identify any specific areas of work that your organization believes should be set aside exclusively for Small Business. 3. Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. 4. Questions regarding this market survey should be addressed to Tyler Martens, Program Manager, 478-955-5165 or via email at tyler.martens.2@us.af.mil. DISCLAIMER: This Request for Information is for market research and planning purposes only. This is not a request for proposal, does not constitute a solicitation, and shall not be construed as a commitment by the government to award a contract. Responses to this RFI are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. The Government will not pay for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of responses. Any information submitted by respondents is strictly voluntary. title: Totalrådgiveraftale vedrørende ombygning og renovering af trænings- og rehabiliteringscenter
description: I forbindelse med regeringens sundhedsreform, skal nogle af Kommunernes ydelser overdrages til Regionerne. Opgaven omfatter totalrådgivning i forbindelse med projektering, myndighedsbehandling, udbud og byggegennemførelse som led i renovering og ombygning af Trænings- og rehabiliteringscentret, Lyngby Hovedgade 1A Ombygningen omfatter blandt andet ombygning af eksisterende træningsarealer til kontorarbejdspladser, etablering og tilpasning af mødefaciliteter, toiletter og personalefunktioner, ny flugtvejstrappe, vurdering og projektering af ventilationsløsninger, afklaring af akustiske forhold samt undersøgelse og håndtering af fugtproblemer. Herudover indgår etablering af ny cykelparkering og mindre arbejder i bygning C.

title: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation - Sole Source - Acquisition of Galley Inserts
description: (i) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; a formal, separate written solicitation document will not be posted publicly. (ii) The solicitation number is FA8641-27-R-B001 and is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP). (iii) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the most recent Federal Acquisition Circular / FAR Deviation Guide updates. (iv) Set-Aside Status: This requirement is not set aside for small business. This is a sole-source solicitation directed to Transtar Aircraft Interiors LLC, Arlington, Texas (CAGE: 8F4J2). (v) Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs): Specific line item structures, quantities, and units of measure are omitted from this public notice and will be provided directly in the RFP to the sole-source vendor. (vi) Description of Requirement: AFLCMC requires customized interior protective stowage inserts intended to provide secure stowage and protection during aircraft operations. The required scope includes the design, fabrication, and delivery of custom protective inserts. (vii) Delivery and Period of Performance: Delivery is estimated at 12 months from contract award, FOB Destination (specific delivery address details will be provided in the RFP). (viii) Justification for Sole Source: Transtar is the only known source with the proprietary technical data and specialized manufacturing capability necessary to satisfy the Government�s requirement within the required schedule. In accordance with FAR 6.305, the Justification & Approval (J&A) document supporting this sole-source selection will be published to sam.gov within 14 days after contract award. (ix) Provisions and Clauses: The standard commercial provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition, include, but not limited to, the equivalents of FAR 52.212-1 (Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services), FAR 52.212-4 (Contract Terms and Conditions), and FAR 52.212-5 (Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders). Specific clauses will be detailed in the direct RFP sent to Transtar Aircraft Interiors LLC. (x) Proposal Submission: While this solicitation is directed as a sole-source procurement to Transtar Aircraft Interiors LLC and is not a request for competitive proposals, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Forest Service, Property and Procurement Services (PPS), Incident Procurement Operations (IPO) intends to issue a Request for Quotation (RFQ) in support of the National Interagency Support Cache (NISC) locations nationwide; essential for storing, tracking, and shipping critical equipment and supplies for wildland fires and all-hazard emergencies. The intent of this solicitation is to provide commercially available freight services, for the delivery of supplies and equipment for all hazardous emergencies, fire and pre-suppression activities, at various locations in the Continental United States and Alaska as directed by the National Interagency Incident Support Caches. title: Preventative Maintenance and Repair of Heavy Equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Philadelphia District, intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Preventative Maintenance and Repair of Heavy Equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office within the USACE Philadelphia (NAP) District area of responsibility in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor is responsible for scheduling work in accordance with the requirements of task order issued and during regular business hours when scheduling on site work. The site conducts regular business from 7:00am to 3:00pm, Monday through Friday, except for federal holidays. All work is to be performed during these regular business hours. Any hours to be worked outside of the regular business hours shall be coordinated with the COR. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform preventative maintenance and repair of heavy equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. The Fort Mifflin Project Office is responsible for the construction of the district�s disposal areas located along the Delaware River. Our mission supports the deepening and the maintenance dredging of the Delaware River and Wilmington Harbor. Heavy Equipment is utilized to construct dikes, ditching for drying and other dirt work. Our equipment is currently composed of D6 Dozers, Excavators (tracks and pontoons), dump trucks (articulated). Without equipment to provide the necessary dirt work in these disposals� areas, dredging assignments in the Delaware Harbor could not be accomplished. It is important that dredging and proper disposal activities of dredge materials is accomplished because it directly effects commerce and the safety of vessels transporting commodities and other resources to the ports. See attachment labeled "W912BU26QA024_FMPO Combined Solicitation Synopsis.pdf" with the requirements of this RFQ and other attachments required for informational and submission purposes. title: Alternative Protein Technologies for Military Field Feeding
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command - Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC) to identify potential sources to provide innovative product development research and/or consumer research and/or demonstration food samples in the area of alternative proteins. Responses are limited to Massachusetts based offerors as determined by CAGE code. The Government requests responders submit a Broad Agency Announcement BAA preproposal as outlined in DEVCOM-SC BAA W911QY-25-R-0023 located at: https://sam.gov/opp/a5ec94e2baee40df9951f864a8665e71/view Please refer to Section VI - Scientific and Technical Areas of Interest, A. Combat Ration Research and Development. Submit the BAA preproposal to: michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil by 23 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. OBJECTIVE: DEVCOM-SC seeks product development, consumer research, and food sample demonstrations of current and emerging novel alternative protein technologies that could be integrated into military rations. BACKGROUND: The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC), Combat Feeding Division (CFD), is seeking information from industry and academia on capabilities related to alternative proteins. The U.S. Army is exploring how the emerging alternative-protein sector can help meet several objectives, including enhancing food supply chain resilience, enabling biomanufacturing of foodstuffs in combat-forward environments, and providing tailored, high-quality nutrition to the Warfighter. DEVCOM-SC CFD has unique expertise in the development and assessment of shelf-stable ration components, as well as food safety and palatability for the Joint Warfighter. We are looking to partner with the commercial and academic sectors to advance technology development in this area. AREAS OF INTEREST: DEVCOM-SC is seeking information from offerors that can provide capabilities in one or more of the following areas. Work proposed should be to advance technology between TRL 4 and 6. Please note, for the purposes of this Sources Sought, we are specifically excluding solutions related to cell-cultured, lab-grown meat or insect protein. Innovative technologies for alternative protein development to reduce Soldier load: Seeking advanced technologies and processes involved in fermentation, precision fermentation, or other novel biomanufacturing methods, that enhance the production of alternative proteins where additional funding in specific components of the research would significantly accelerate advancements in technology between TRL 4 and 6, enabling faster transition to operational use. These technologies should focus on creating lightweight and nutrient-dense ration solutions to reduce logistical burdens and physical load on warfighters while maintaining or enhancing nutritional value and operational performance. Innovative Product Development: The development of innovative meat-alternative products specifically designed for inclusion in military rations, meeting stringent requirements for nutrition, shelf stability, and palatability. Consumer Research and Acceptability: The ability to conduct comprehensive consumer research (e.g., focus groups, sensory panels, field testing) to enhance the acceptability and consumption of alternative proteins within a military population. Food Sample Demonstration: An optional addition to the effort would be to provide 100 food samples of a potential product that has Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) status with an FDA no-questions letter to demonstrate the maturation of an alternative protein manufacturing technology. These samples would be provided to the Government for sensory acceptability and other performance characteristics and will be consumed by our test panel of experts. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested parties (companies or academic institutions) are requested to submit a proposal that details their capabilities in one or more of the areas listed in Section 3.0. Submissions should include: A detailed description of your technical approach. Relevant past performance or corporate experience. A rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimate for the proposed work or samples. This information will be used for market research and planning purposes. Responses to this Sources Sought are not binding proposals, but they will help shape future solicitation requirements. Offerors are welcome to send samples at their own cost for evaluation. DEVCOM SC will not return any items, nor is DEVCOM SC obligated to share any data from evaluation. Sending samples is not required for consideration for funding. Samples must be GRAS with an FDA no-questions letter. Please coordinate by e-mail (richard.j.green.civ@army.mil) before sending samples. Address information will be provided at that time. SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This Sources Sought Announcement is issued solely for information and planning purposes and to identify interested sources. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. No contract will be awarded from this announcement. This Sources Sought does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. It is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. Further, unsolicited proposals will not be accepted. Funding is not available at this time. The United States Army has not made a commitment to procure any of the items/services discussed, and release of this Sources Sought Announcement should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. Response to this Sources Sought Announcement is voluntary and no reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this and any follow-on information requests. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Sources Sought Announcement does not preclude participation in any future RFP if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential responders to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this subject. RESPONSES: Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by sending BAA preproposals regarding this requirement to DEVCOM-SC via e-mail ONLY to michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil by 23 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Notice. All costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the expense of the interested party. Submissions should include: Whether you are proposing product development and/or consumer research and/or sample demonstration. A detailed description of your technical approach. Relevant past performance or corporate experience. A rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimate for the proposed work or samples. Please provide business size (indicate your socioeconomic status), applicable NAICS code, and CAGE code. QUESTIONS: Any questions for clarification may be emailed to michael.s.wiederoder.civ@army.mil, richard.j.green.civ@army.mil and jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil no later than 18 November 2026, 5:00 PM EST. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. An unattributed list of questions and answers will be published at the same web location of this Sources Sought Announcement.
